company_name: Huaxin Building Materials Group Co., Ltd. (formerly Huaxin Cement)

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR +6.3% diverges by more than 30% from EPS 5-yr CAGR -12.6%: FY2020 was the peak of the Chinese cement cycle (net income RMB5.6bn vs RMB2.9bn in FY2025), so EPS-based growth is a peak-to-trough read and equity CAGR understates the forward overseas ramp. The base path starts at the FY2026 guidance (+15%) and decelerates to 2.5%.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; no interest strip, net borrower): FY2020 4,816; FY2021 1,366; FY2022 -3,199; FY2023 1,355; FY2024 1,416; FY2025 4,069. The 3-yr owner-FCF CAGR is undefined (FY2022 base negative at the trough of the capex cycle and domestic price collapse); 5-yr is -3.3%. SBC is immaterial, so the owner-FCF and reported-FCF series are within 0.2% of each other. FCF history is driven by the capex cycle (FY2022 capex RMB7.7bn) rather than by operations: OCF has stayed within RMB4.6-8.4bn every year.

scenario_narratives.base: Huaxin delivers the FY2026 plan: revenue clears RMB40bn (+15%) as the Nigeria, Mozambique, Tanzania and Zimbabwe capacity comes on stream and overseas EBITDA passes RMB7bn, then growth fades to mid-single digits by FY2028 because the ~60% of revenue tied to Chinese cement, clinker and ready-mix keeps shrinking 3-5% a year while aggregates and overseas grow. Group EBITDA margin drifts from 26% to 28% purely on mix (overseas gross margins are roughly double domestic), with no domestic price recovery assumed. The RMB15bn FY2026 capex programme is charged at ~83% execution and capex converges on D&A by FY2032, so owner FCF is negative in FY2026 and only reaches a mature ~RMB5bn+ run rate from FY2029. NCI leakage (~18%) and a 27-28% effective tax rate are charged in the flows; net debt of ~RMB18bn at March 2026 is deducted. Terminal value is capped at 12x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Both engines fire. Overseas: the African and Central Asian plants ramp ahead of schedule, Lafarge Africa's naira-denominated pricing holds, further bolt-ons add capacity at sensible multiples, and overseas becomes ~45% of revenue by FY2028 at 35%+ EBITDA margins. Domestic: 'organise production by approved capacity', carbon trading and ultra-low-emission mandates force marginal capacity out and domestic cement prices recover 10-15% from the 2025 trough, lifting group EBITDA margin to ~31% -- still below the FY2020 peak of 33%. Revenue grows 17%/11%/8% over FY2026-28 and capex intensity normalises a year earlier than base. Terminal growth 3% (EM mix) with the same 12x cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: The overseas pivot proves harder than the slide deck: Nigerian FX devaluation, political scrutiny of the Lafarge Africa deal, cost over-runs on greenfield lines in Mozambique and Zimbabwe, and an over-paid acquisition or two mean the RMB15bn is spent but EBITDA lags (capex 24% of revenue in FY2026 with margins falling to 23.5%). Domestically, anti-involution again fails to translate into pricing power, demand keeps falling with real estate, and ready-mix receivables consume working capital (-5% capture). Revenue growth collapses to ~0-2% from FY2028 and the EBITDA margin settles at 24%, below FY2025. With ~RMB18bn of net debt the equity is a thin slice: this path produces a sharply lower but still positive value, so the business survives it, but the balance sheet leaves little margin for a second mistake.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A cyclical, levered, SBC-zero industrial valued on unlevered owner FCF built from components, with the FY2026 capex supercycle charged explicitly rather than hidden in a flat margin, NCI and tax charged once as a combined leakage driver, leases held as debt, a CNY-built WACC applied uniformly, and a 12x cap on the terminal multiple. Risk is priced in the scenario weights (30/50/20), not in an ad-hoc discount-rate premium. The H-share trades at a ~42% discount to the A-share line, so the HKD quote is already the cheaper claim on the same cash flows.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex execution: RMB15bn FY2026 programme (42% of revenue) with net debt already ~RMB18bn; a slip in overseas EBITDA delivery leaves the leverage without the cash flow
Frontier-market FX and political risk (Nigeria naira, Mozambique, Zimbabwe, Central Asia) on ~33% and rising share of revenue
Domestic China cement demand in structural decline (2025 output a 15-year low); base case assumes no price recovery, bull case needs one
NCI leakage is modelled at ~18% of unlevered profit; overseas growth in partly-owned subsidiaries could lift it
H1 2026 interim balance sheet not in the folder: net debt anchor is 31 Mar 2026 and will rise as the capex programme is funded
Terminal value capped at 12x owner FCF; a Chinese cement producer may be awarded less by the market (sector EV/EBITDA 5-7x)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for 6655.HK at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 11.35-20.20 HKD. FX from Yahoo CNYHKD=X; A-share parity from 600801.SS.
data_sources.financials: 6655.HK_Metrics.csv (FY2020-FY2025 annual + interims, RMB millions) built from the HKEX annual reports; FY2025 AR consolidated statements and notes V.1, V.28, V.57-59; Q1 2026 quarterly report balance sheet (31 Mar 2026).
data_sources.qualitative: 6655.HK_Analysis.json (business mix, overseas M&A, guidance, bull/bear axes) and the FY2025 AR outlook and business-plan sections.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: FY2025 AR note V.58 adjusted weighted-average 2,075,331,794 (basic 2,072,571,683 + 2,760,111 restricted-stock dilution). Issued capital 2,078,995,649 A+H shares less ~5.9m treasury A shares held for ESOPs. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows (immaterial) and buybacks only recycle shares into the restricted-stock plans.
inputs.debt_composition: 31 Mar 2026 (Q1 2026 report, latest balance sheet in the folder): short-term borrowings 582.6 + current portion of non-current liabilities 5,166.7 (bonds, LT loans, finance-lease payables and lease liabilities due within one year) + long-term borrowings 13,805.5 + bonds payable 5,242.5 + non-current lease liabilities 878.7 + long-term payables 1,096.4 (sale-and-leaseback / financial leasing per FY2025 MD&A) = 26,772. Cash and bank balances 8,731.1 (FY2025 note V.1 shows the 'other cash' component is short-dated time deposits, not restricted cash, so the full balance is counted). H1 2026 results (Aug 2026) are referenced in the Analysis JSON but the interim filing is not in Extracted/, so the Q1 2026 balance sheet is the anchor.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 OCF 6,694.0 less purchase of fixed/intangible/other long-term assets 2,620.0. PRC-GAAP OCF is pre-interest (interest paid sits in financing), so this is an unlevered flow. FY2025 organic capex was abnormally low because RMB5.76bn of acquisitions (Lafarge Africa, Brazil EMBU) and RMB2.23bn of investment payments were booked outside the capex line; the forward capex path normalises this (see assumptions).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR consolidated cash flow note, share-based payments RMB4.78m (CSV StockBasedComp). Effectively an SBC-zero filer: restricted-stock ESOPs are funded from repurchased A shares.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income RMB205.4m is left inside the flows because the company is a net borrower (net debt ~RMB18bn); the interest-income strip applies only to net-cash companies.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases RMB62.2m of A shares, all granted to restricted-stock incentive participants -- a recycling mechanism, not a count-reducing buyback.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX H-share quote in HKD. fx_rate is HKD per CNY = 1.1746 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-23). Parity check: the A-share line 600801.SS closed at RMB22.85 on 2026-10-23 = HK$26.84 at this rate versus the H-share quote -- a ~42% H-share discount, which is normal for A/H dual listings (H discount, not a currency error; the direction is confirmed by the A share converting to a larger HKD number). Per-share values are computed in CNY and converted to HKD; the unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are in HKD, CNY twins are suffixed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows. Cost of equity ~10.5%: China 10-yr CGB ~1.8% + beta 1.1 x 6.5% China/EM equity risk premium + ~1.5% premium for the growing frontier-market (Nigeria, Mozambique, Tanzania, Zimbabwe, Central Asia) earnings mix. After-tax cost of debt ~3.5% (RMB bonds 2-3% coupons blended with USD acquisition loans). Market-value weights ~65/35 equity/debt (market cap ~RMB28bn at the H-share price against ~RMB18bn net debt) give WACC = 0.65 x 10.5 + 0.35 x 3.5 = 8.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality and execution risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities (non-current 878.7 + the current portion inside current non-current liabilities) and the financial-leasing long-term payables are included in total_debt; lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows, and right-of-use renewal is covered by the capex path (which converges on D&A, itself inclusive of ROU depreciation). Applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests (RMB5,128m book at 31 Mar 2026; RMB742.5m or ~21% of FY2025 net profit, concentrated in the overseas subsidiaries such as HBM Nigeria ~83%-owned) are charged ONCE, in the flows: cash_tax_rate_path is a combined income-tax-plus-NCI leakage driver. FY2025 effective income tax 28.5% (RMB1,412m on PBT 4,950m; above the 25% statutory because of unrecognised deferred tax on loss-making domestic subsidiaries and withholding tax on overseas dividends) combined with ~18% NCI leakage on unlevered after-tax profit gives 1 - 0.715 x 0.82 = ~41%. Calibration: FY2025 EBIT 5,538 x (1 - 0.41) = 3,267 vs attributable net income 2,853 + after-tax interest expense ~567 = 3,420 (within 5%). No NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US / cyclical') with the adaptations file applied: currency-matched CNY WACC, HKD quote bridge, leases as debt, NCI as a leakage driver, SBC-zero. Huaxin is an operating cement / aggregates / ready-mix producer (China ~67% of revenue, overseas ~33% and growing fast) -- not a financial, REIT, holdco or distressed shell. FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end). The investment thesis is the pivot from a structurally shrinking Chinese cement market to higher-margin frontier-market cement; the valuation therefore hinges on (1) the overseas capacity ramp converting the ~RMB15bn FY2026 capex programme into EBITDA, and (2) whether domestic 'anti-involution' supply discipline stabilises Chinese prices. Both are modelled in the scenario paths. The FY2025 reported FCF of RMB4.07bn is NOT a repeatable base: organic capex was only 7.4% of revenue because growth capital went through the acquisition line; the base case charges 22% of revenue in FY2026 (~RMB9bn against the RMB15bn plan, assuming the ~83% historical execution rate and that part of the Nigeria/Brazil consideration was already paid in 2025 and sits in Q1 2026 net debt), fading to 10% by FY2031. Year-1 owner FCF is therefore negative in all scenarios -- a capex supercycle, not distress. Working-capital capture 0%: payables (RMB8.2bn) exceed receivables + notes + inventory (RMB7.4bn), so growth is roughly supplier-funded. House and street bases coincide (SBC ~0.01% of revenue): band_position is degenerate and should be read as n/a. Terminal cap 12x owner FCF, the low end of the cyclical range, for a cement producer whose sector trades at 5-7x EV/EBITDA. Analysis JSON was present and used for the scenario axes.

bear.narrative: Frontier-market execution stumbles while the domestic decline continues.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +15%: guidance 'exceed RMB40bn' (+13%) and H1 2026 revenue +21.5% with a tougher H2 comp once Lafarge Africa (consolidated from Aug 2025) annualises. FY2027-28 +8%/+6% as Nigeria upgrades, Mozambique, Tanzania and Zimbabwe lines reach full-year output and Brazil aggregates ramp; thereafter overseas growth of high-single digits is netted against a domestic cement/RMX base shrinking ~3-5% a year, converging on 2.5% nominal.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 EBITDA margin 26.0%. Mix shift toward overseas (gross margin ~42% vs ~20s domestically; overseas EBITDA guided >RMB7bn in FY2026) lifts the group margin ~2pp over three years; domestic held flat (no anti-involution price recovery assumed in base).
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 22% of revenue (~RMB9bn executed of the RMB15bn plan incl. M&A), 16% and 13% in FY2027-28 as the Africa build-out completes, converging on D&A (~10%) from FY2032 -- a mature cement producer replaces roughly what it depreciates.
base.tax_rationale: Combined income tax + NCI leakage: 28.5% effective tax easing to ~27% as domestic loss subsidiaries' unrecognised losses are utilised, NCI ~18% of unlevered after-tax profit, combined 41% -> 40%.

bull.narrative: Overseas ramp beats plan and domestic supply discipline finally bites.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: net debt has doubled in two years to fund frontier-market M&A (goodwill +260%), FY2026 adds another RMB15bn of capex at a ~54% asset-liability ratio, and the domestic cement market is in structural decline -- a leverage-plus-execution risk the flows cannot fully carry. Bull cut to 20% because it needs two independent things to go right at once: an on-time overseas ramp AND a domestic pricing recovery that has been promised for years without arriving. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
